title: High TPS rollover and seamless fallback demo - QuantaHealth

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood Product), Liam (QuantaHealth CTO), Hannah (ML Eng), Marcus (SRE), Priya (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): walked through rollover, fallback and TTL behavior. Demoed console traces and Optimize recommendations. Agreed pilot and follow-ups.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through a focused demo on how Redwood handles very high TPS with long conversations and the streaming path when the system hits backpressure — hi Liam, Hannah
[00:12] Liam: hey thanks, excited to see how we can avoid the user-facing slowdowns during our morning surge, we get spiky traffic from the triage flow
[00:20] Jared: yep, so quick note on agenda, we'll show a live load run, then Console traces, and finally Optimize suggestions and a canary/fallback policy example
[00:32] Marcus: uh just to flag from SRE perspective we care about graceful degradation not silent failures, ideally a fast 503 fallback than long tail latency
[00:45] Maya: absolutely — that's the core of the rollover demo, we'll show fallback tiers: same model smaller instance, alternative quantized variant, and region failover with preserved session semantics
[01:05] Hannah: real quick, our sessions average 12k tokens but some clinician sessions hit 80k, and we use KV context stitching. Will you show how KV eviction interacts with fallbacks?
[01:22] Jared: yes, good callout. We'll demonstrate prefix cache hits, then a forced eviction scenario. In the fallback case we keep KV references and stitch with partial history where possible, we also show TTL-based streaming dropback
[01:40] Speaker 1: okay great
[01:52] (demo starts — load generator connecting)
[02:05] Jared: kicking off the high TPS generator now, target 900 reqs/s with a 3s average prompt length — this is similar to your morning triage pattern right?
[02:18] Liam: yeah that's close, although we do short bursts up to 1.6k rps for a couple minutes
[02:30] Jared: rolling. console shows overall token throughput increase — highlighting the per-route latency histogram
[02:45] Maya: note the orange bars on the Console dashboard are our latency p50/p95 — you can see at 700rps p95 is still under target but once we push it we start to see streaming stalls
[03:05] Marcus: what does a streaming stall look like for the client SDK? is it chunked pauses or full connection resets?
[03:18] Jared: mostly you'll see paused chunks (partial frames) while the runtime backpressure queues; we do keep the streaming socket open with periodic heartbeats, but the client SDK can optionally fallback to poll mode if consistent pauses exceed the TTL threshold
[03:35] Hannah: TTL threshold? can you explain that mapping to our SLA?
[03:42] Sofia: sure, TTL is a per-session config for how long we tolerate streaming silence before we tear down and either retry against a fallback or return a lightweight summary. It's adjustable per-route; by default we recommend 8s for interactive flows, shorter for chatty token-by-token UIs
[04:00] Liam: and the fallback — that's where you switch to a smaller model or other region?
[04:06] Jared: yeah we have ordered fallback policies: 1) same region, quantized variant, 2) same region, smaller architecture (faster but less context), 3) cross-region instance (if configured), 4) degrade to cached completion/summary. The Console shows exactly which step was taken in traces
[04:25] Hannah: curious about token accounting when you fallback mid-session — are we billed twice for the overlapping prefixes?
[04:33] Maya: we surface token counts per model and we don't double-bill the same token; we credit prefix reuse via our KV cache accounting. But if you choose to re-request full context against a new model you'll see both calls' tokens — Optimize will suggest prefix reuse to avoid that
[04:50] Jared: starting a forced eviction now — pushing memory pressure to the KV cache to demonstrate eviction rules
[05:05] (brief noise, keyboard clatter)
[05:20] Jared: console trace annotated: you can see the KV cache hit rate drops from 92% to 37% as we evict entries older than TTL. At this point, the fallback policy chooses the quantized variant in the same region
[05:38] Marcus: will that quantized variant preserve the same API shape? our client assumes same output format
[05:45] Jared: yes we deploy variants that are compatible at the API level; function calling and structured outputs are preserved — subtle quality differences can happen; Optimize will flag expected regressions on the eval set
[06:03] Hannah: are there any pitfalls with prefix stitching when history is partially missing? We need deterministic behavior for audit trails
[06:12] Sofia: we append a provenance header to the response when history was stitched or truncated, and the trace in Console shows which chunks were used. For audits we can export the session reconstruction along with hashes of truncated chunks
[06:30] Liam: that helps. Another question: how fast is the region failover in practice? we can't afford multi-second session loss for critical flows
[06:40] Jared: region failover is generally last resort — if you have cross-region configured and warm replicas, we see ~800-1200ms handoff in our tests. But that's dependent on networking; for sub-1s failover you'd need warm dedicated pools and the Console's rollout controls help orchestrate that
[06:58] Maya: demo note: we'll show two fallback traces, one where we stay in-region and one where we cross-region
[07:10] (loading trace 1)
[07:22] Jared: trace 1: in-region quantized fallback at 740rps. You can see streaming pauses at [07:28] while the runtime swaps execution kernels and switches the request to a quantized container — there's a ~200-400ms window of paused chunks
[07:45] Hannah: do you surface that as an event for our telemetry? we need to correlate it with our clickstream
[07:52] Jared: yes, span events and logs are exported to your OTEL collector; we can also attach route-level tags so you can filter fallbacks in your analytics
[08:05] Marcus: any weird interactions with our rate-limiter? we use token-bucket shapers upstream
[08:12] Maya: Redwood's routing happens post-ingress; we can accept a rate-limited frontdoor or plug into your existing shaper with our configurable throttle hints. For spikes we recommend a thin frontdoor that lets Redwood decide per-token batching and fallback
[08:30] (pause, switch to trace 2 - cross-region)
[08:40] Jared: trace 2 induced cross-region failover — notice Console shows session handoff and a session-id mapping. There's an authorization hop for the private control plane which adds a small latent window
[08:55] Liam: hmm auth hop — we need to know what credentials cross-region requires. We prefer no cross-region for PHI in our EU tenants
[09:04] Maya: understood — cross-region only when explicitly enabled and subject to your compliance rules; for PHI you'd likely want Private with VPC peering and no cross-region fallback configured
[09:16] Hannah: I noticed earlier you mentioned the SDK can fallback to poll mode if streaming stalls. Is that client-side feature released?
[09:24] Jared: it's in SDK v1.8, opt-in. Poll mode opens resilient retry logic and avoids holding sockets. For mobile clients we often recommend poll mode plus lightweight streaming heartbeats
[09:38] (demo: enable SDK poll fallback)
[09:45] Jared: flipping the TTL down to 3s now to simulate aggressive tear-downs — you'll see the session drop and then a quick retry against a cached summary response
[10:02] Priya: from procurement, curious how we measure the cost delta between always-on dedicated pools vs these fallback behaviors
[10:11] Sofia: Optimize can run a simulated cost analysis over your routes: it models expected traffic, batching, and cache hit rates to recommend a hybrid: reserved baseline with burst-only dedicated; the Console then projects monthly savings and SLA impact
[10:28] Liam: can we see a sample Optimize recommendation in this session?
[10:33] Maya: yes, we preloaded a sample suggestion for your triage route — opening Optimize panel
[10:40] (screen share of Optimize)
[10:46] Jared: Optimize suggests enabling prefix caching for repetitive prompts, increasing batch window from 25ms to 40ms for that route, and enabling a 4-bit quantized variant for non-PII flows; net estimate: 32% token-cost savings at 5% latency increase on p95
[11:02] Hannah: 4-bit quantization worries me for hallucinations on clinical text — do you have evals we can share?
[11:09] Sofia: yes, we attach evals and expected quality deltas for your prompt set. For critical flows you can opt to keep a non-quantized golden path and route less-critical requests to quantized variants
[11:24] (noise, typing)
[11:40] Jared: next I'll demo a long-context stitching example where we intentionally truncate middle chunks and stitch the most relevant context via similarity search against the KV store
[11:52] (load generator simulates long 80k token session)
[12:05] Jared: see here, we use a sliding window and chunk-level embeddings to pick top-k context pieces — when we fall back during eviction we send only the top 10 relevant chunks which preserves intent in 85% of cases in our evals
[12:26] Hannah: how do you guarantee determinism for audit? if chunk selection is heuristic we need consistent hashes
[12:33] Jared: we persist the chunk selection indices in session metadata so you can reconstruct the exact set used — Console export includes the chunk ids and hashed payload snapshot for audit purposes
[12:50] Liam: ok that's reassuring. Marcus, any SRE red flags so far?
[12:56] Marcus: door looks good, but want restoration behavior after a crash — do you support session replay or queued requests?
[13:05] Jared: we have optional request replay where unacked tokens are replayed against the same model up to a TTL; for longer, you can opt-in to durable session storage where the KV store is persisted to your S3 or your VPC-backed store
[13:21] Maya: dropping a link in chat to replay and durable storage docs — (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/replay-durable)
[13:30] Priya: procurement question again — for a pilot do we need any legal addendum to enable dedicated burst pools?
[13:38] Maya: we'll send a standard pilot agreement plus an addendum for data processing and private deployment options if required
[13:45] (demo continues — simulating a spike to 1.2k rps)
[14:02] Jared: pushing to 1.2k rps — observe graceful shedding: lower-priority routes are auto-throttled, and fallbacks are triggered for the triage route to preserve overall system stability
[14:20] Hannah: can you label route priority via headers? we want to mark clinician flows as high-priority
[14:28] Jared: yes, route priority can be set via routing tags or JWT claims; Console has a priority matrix. We'll show that in the runbook export
[14:38] (pause)
[15:00] Jared: small hiccup — one of the quantized variants rebooted in the pool, you can see the container restart event in the trace, fallback chain continued to the next variant, client saw a short 220ms pause
[15:16] Liam: what's the MTTI for those container reboots, are they common?
[15:22] Jared: rare in our fleets — we generally have auto-heal and warm spare containers; when you reserve dedicated pools those spares can be provisioned per-customer for tighter MTTI
[15:35] Sofia: also note that the Console can show heatmap of restarts; Optimize flags problematic models with suggested kernel changes or alternate compilers
[15:46] (crosstalk)
[16:00] Maya: quick poll — would you prefer we prototype warm dedicated burst capacity for the pilot or rely on hosted with strict fallbacks?
[16:09] Liam: pilot should be hosted first; if the numbers match we'll move to dedicated burst for mornings
[16:15] Priya: procurement prefers staged commitment before signing for dedicated pools
[16:21] Maya: makes sense. We'll propose a 2-week hosted pilot with optional reserved burst windows.
[16:29] (switch to question/answer)
[16:35] Marcus: security: can you confirm encryption in transit + KMS integration for session keys?
[16:42] Jared: yes, TLS for in-transit. For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM; keys for cached context are encrypted with customer-managed keys when you choose that option
[16:58] Hannah: does KV stored context ever leave our VPC in Private mode?
[17:05] Sofia: no, in Private the KV store stays in your network; in hosted we use encrypted multi-tenant stores but you can request customer isolation for sensitive tenants
[17:18] Liam: for PHI we will want Private on-prem or VPC + HSM; let's scope that after pilot
[17:26] Maya: noted — will include Private deployment checklist in follow-up
[17:34] (demo: show runbook export)
[17:45] Jared: runbook export includes threshold values: p95 latency trigger 1.2s, KV miss rate > 40% triggers eviction policy review, fallback rate > 2% triggers alert to SRE
[18:02] Marcus: can alerts be delivered via PagerDuty?
[18:07] Jared: yes, integrated with PD and Slack, and you can route to specific escalation policies per service
[18:15] Hannah: last technical question — how do you test for hallucination differentials between quantized and full models?
[18:24] Sofia: we run parallel evals on your prompt set and report classification/QA metrics; Optimize surfaces degradation per prompt type with suggested mitigations like output filters or tuned system prompts
[18:40] (wrap-up section)
[18:45] Maya: quick recap — 1) we demonstrated high TPS generator and console traces, 2) showed fallback chain behavior and TTL-based streaming tear-downs, 3) walked through Optimize recommendations and cost tradeoffs, 4) covered security/compliance and private deployment options
[19:04] Liam: this was really helpful, thanks. A few items for us: Hannah will gather prompt samples and we'll look at pilot dates
[19:12] Priya: procurement will need the pricing sheet and pilot terms before we can approve
[19:20] Maya: I'll send pricing and the SOC2 + architecture docs by Monday. We'll also include a sample benchmark CSV and a suggested pilot plan for your morning surge window
[19:34] Jared: action: I'll run the 100k-token streaming test on staging with sample prompts once Hannah shares them
[19:45] (meeting ending, casual closers)
[19:52] Liam: great thanks everyone
[19:55] Maya: thanks all, talk soon
